The playground had been nestled in the center of a flat land, far from the hill where the school was. You had the school itself that set up on this hill, and behind it, we had the doors that lead to the playground. So, as you went out the door, there was a dip in landscape and right on the flat-lands there it was.

At this time, I remember that we didn't have anything fenced off, so kids could wonder off into the woods, but we had enough sense not to. She raised a dark brow. "What sort of game?"

"I don't know. Something with adventure, and traveling."

"We have computers for that." Estela snapped back, rolling her eyes and blowing a puff of hair out of her face.

"Computers? Nothing beats the great outdoors, Stela! I was thinking something like ... world travelers."

"Like Carmen Sandiego?"

"Nothing like Carmen--listen! We'd travel to different dimensions and worlds using our imagination and stuff. It would be something of our own creation. Cool, right?"

She stared off. "Sounds boring, man."

"It'd be like ... um, um, Stargate!"

"That has to do with time traveling *and* dimensional traveling, Kera."

I groaned. "Come on, it'd be the coolest thing. You know you wanna play it."

Estela squinted at me for a minute, contemplating the offer and eventually sighed. "Okay, fine. One condition."

"What's that?"

"No one else can know we're playing this. It'd ruin the fun."

I grinned. "Duh, you doofus!"

We laughed as the bell rung for us to go back inside, but the next day we were ready to play. Although, there would eventually be four of us in total later on. The first time we played, it was really awkward, but we eventually got around to a solid foundation. They were the best times of my life, and I loved ever second of it. "Go on without me!" She cried out in exaggeration, throwing arm and making a face.

We finally 'made it' back to the entry point to the dimension, and we both fell to the grass laughing. Just two third graders having fun. No harm in that, right?

Never one to back down from a dare, Bryce went down the path in search for the ball. He walked around for a bit and finally managed to get it. When he turned to look around, he didn't know where he was and there was yelling, incomprehensible yelling and screeching. It started off as a low hum, and got louder the longer he stayed until the voices were practically clawing at the insides of his ear. He took off when he heard a branch break, dropped the football right where he had found it. Right before he got to the clearing where he could see people, he said something pierced his ankle and it made him stumble forward and fall. He didn't know what it was until one of the guys ran over to help him up off the ground.

Me and Estela were silent when he told us this, sharing looks of concerned. She told me that what he described was what she had visualized and saw when being chased by the natives in the jungle, if not similar, it was *exact*. We held off from playing the game for a few months and just jump-roped. Bryce ended up with a cast on his legs, and we were back to our boring selves. They fenced off the shrubbery of trees after that.

A few days after that, we found the football mauled and inside one of the tire castles. We stayed away from down there for a good while. Everyone did. Soon, though, we forgot about it and went back to being active climbers and swingers. Though, neither I or Estela brought up the Dimension Game anymore. It was then, that the dreams started. I would go to sleep and ... immediately wake up to a place foreign to where I had previously been. Sometimes, I wouldn't even sleep, because I was scared that if I did, I wouldn't be able to come back here. It was just that surreal to me.

I would lay down in our plane of existence, and just as soon as I closed my eyes, I would wake up in another. The soul cannot be seen without a body, so I always assumed that it was astral projection when I started doing research.

That didn't add up. The next possible thing was that I had multiple bodies in these ... places, and that's how I kept waking up there. The same places that me and Estela had 'imagined' up when we first started playing the Dimension Game. Memories of later incidents are still a little blurry, but that's the gist of what we both can remember at the moment.
